originalTitle: Wildfires in south-west France flare up as region braces for new 40C heatwave
summary: Firefighters are braced for a sharp rise in temperatures on Wednesday, which could complicate the containment of wildfires in Gironde.
content:
The race to stop the French woodland fires in their tracks

Firefighters in France are working around the clock to contain wildfires that have been raging in the Gironde region, while bracing for another sharp rise in temperatures.

"The fire is like David against Goliath," said Eric Brocardi, spokesman of the national firefighters' federation.

Four of his colleagues had died in recent weeks across France, he said, and 2,000 had been deployed in the Gironde to contain the flames, which for days have ravaged the countryside between the coastline and Bordeaux.

According to regional prefect Sophie Brocas 14 places that had already been hit by the fires saw new flare-ups on Tuesday. "We are not in the clear," she said.

This summer's fourth heatwave was expected to start by Wednesday, bringing temperatures in the area to 40C.

Similar temperatures are expected in Spain.

Dozens of communities are still threatened by wildfires that forced more than 70,000 to evacuate their homes over the last week - although many have now been allowed back.

The Madrid region has been especially affected, but Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said while there were highly challenging hours and days ahead, light was beginning to appear "at the end of the tunnel".

In neighbouring Portugal, 400 firefighters were tackling a large fire on three active fronts in the eastern Guarda area.

The French city of Bordeaux is not currently under threat, according to officials, despite the fact that one of the wildfires burning on Monday came only 15km (9 miles) from the city's periphery.

But Commander Rémi Lassoureille, who is leading the firefighting response in the Gironde region, is still worried.

"We are frightened about the impact on Bordeaux and the metropolitan area," he said. Air quality in the city also deteriorated greatly.

"By Sunday evening everything had really begun to empty out," a holidaymaker from Essex told the BBC, adding that the air was "really smoky" with bits of ash. "People were staying indoors, so it was eerie, and very sad."

People wearing masks in Bordeaux due to the smoke. "The fire is like David against Goliath," said the French firefighters' federation

The majority of residents and tourists were wearing masks and the smell of smoke clung on to clothes for days, she said.

A firefighter "got a round of applause" as he walked through the Marché des Chartrons in Bordeaux where restaurants were having to close their doors because of the ash in the air, she added.

"The city has been very quiet," said Graham White, president of the Bordeaux British Community. "The shops, restaurants and cafes are fairly empty... Interestingly on Sunday when there was still smoke, there were people brave enough to sit outside on terraces."

White, who has been living in the area for several years, said this sort of event was "something significant".

But some news reports had suggested the situation in Bordeaux was "akin to being the next Great Fire of London", which was not the case, White added.

Health Minister Stéphanie Rist said the government was being "very vigilant" in terms of air pollution and urged people in the affected areas to stay indoors.

On Tuesday morning the Gironde prefect ordered a new evacuation of all camping sites near the coast at Lacanau, while those in the nearby town were allowed to stay put but told to prepare for sudden evacuation.

About 4,000 tourists told to leave the area are in addition to the 220,000 people evacuated around France in recent days.

An estimated 240 homes and houses have been destroyed, officials have said.

By midday on Tuesday firefighters were already intervening in various parts of the region to tackle fires that were picking up again.

A 23-year-old man who was arrested on suspicion of starting a fire in the Var region. is now facing 15 years' imprisonment. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said that 184 people had been arrested since 6 July in connection with the fires.

A message to firefighters in the Biscarrosse area, south-west of Bordeaux

Peggy Plouhinec, the general director of Château Picque Caillou - one of the few wine estates on the west side of Bordeaux - told the BBC that her business chose to close at the weekend because of the smoke, but that the situation had improved since then and that a bout of rain on Sunday night had helped.

While her vineyards were not at risk, she said tourists had "deserted" the region.

"The hospitality sector will be impacted this summer, that's for sure," she added. "What is happening is unprecedented. We're lucky that we haven't been too affected yet, but the business will still suffer from the lower numbers of tourists."

"But many people have lost their homes or their businesses, not to mention the firefighters who have been hard at work for weeks now and who must be exhausted."

One resident of Cap Ferret, which was evacuated late last week, told French media that his main concern now was for the peninsula he lived in, rather than the big city city inland.

"Everyone talks about saving Bordeaux, but in Bordeaux there's nothing but concrete. Have you ever seen concrete burn?"

"Here, there are only trees... and when you see all that has burned, it's a catastrophe."

Additional reporting by Xavier Pallas

chineseTitle: 法国西南部野火爆发，该地区正准备迎接新的40摄氏度热浪
chineseSummary: 周三，消防队员准备应对气温急剧上升的情况，这可能会使吉伦特省野火的控制变得更加复杂。
chineseContent:
阻止法国林地火灾的竞赛

法国消防队员正在全天候工作，以遏制吉伦特省肆虐的野火，同时准备迎接气温的再次急剧上升。

“这场大火就像大卫对抗歌利亚，”全国消防员联合会发言人埃里克·布罗卡迪说。

他说，最近几周，他的四名同事在法国各地丧生，并在吉伦特省部署了 2,000 名同事来控制火势，几天来，火势已经肆虐了海岸线和波尔多之间的乡村。

据地区长官索菲·布罗卡斯 (Sophie Brocas) 称，周二，已经遭受火灾的 14 个地方又出现了新的火灾。 “我们还不清楚，”她说。

今年夏天的第四次热浪预计将于周三开始，使该地区气温达到 40 摄氏度。

预计西​​班牙也将出现类似的气温。

数十个社区仍然受到野火的威胁，上周迫使超过 70,000 人撤离家园，尽管许多人现已获准返回。

马德里地区受到的影响尤其严重，但总理佩德罗·桑切斯表示，尽管未来数小时和数天都将面临高度挑战，但“隧道尽头”已经开始出现曙光。

在邻国葡萄牙，400 名消防员正在瓜尔达东部地区的三个活跃战线上扑灭大火。

据官员称，法国波尔多市目前并未受到威胁，尽管周一燃烧的一场野火距离该市外围仅 15 公里（9 英里）。

但负责吉伦特省消防救援工作的指挥官雷米·拉苏雷耶 (Rémi Lassoureille) 仍然感到担忧。

“我们担心这对波尔多和大都市区的影响，”他说。城市空气质量也大幅恶化。

一位来自埃塞克斯的度假者告诉英国广播公司：“到周日晚上，一切都开始变得空虚。”他补充说，空气中“真的烟雾缭绕”，还夹杂着一些灰烬。 “人们都呆在室内，所以这很奇怪，也很悲伤。”

由于烟雾，波尔多的人们戴着口罩。法国消防员联合会表示：“这场大火就像大卫对抗歌利亚”

她说，大多数居民和游客都戴着口罩，衣服上好几天都留着烟味。

她补充说，一名消防员走过波尔多的夏特龙市场时“获得了热烈的掌声”，那里的餐馆因空气中的火山灰而不得不关门。

“这座城市一直非常安静，”波尔多英国社区主席格雷厄姆怀特说。 “商店、餐馆和咖啡馆相当空……有趣的是，周日仍有烟雾时，有人勇敢地坐在外面的露台上。”

怀特已经在该地区生活了几年，他说此类事件“意义重大”。

但怀特补充说，一些新闻报道称波尔多的情况“类似于伦敦的下一场大火”，但事实并非如此。

卫生部长斯蒂芬妮·里斯特表示，政府对空气污染“非常警惕”，并敦促受影响地区的人们呆在室内。

周二早上，吉伦特省省长下令对拉卡诺海岸附近的所有露营地进行新的疏散，而附近城镇的露营地则被允许留在原地，但被告知要为突然疏散做好准备。

除了最近几天在法国各地疏散的 22 万人之外，还有大约 4,000 名游客被告知离开该地区。

官员称，估计有 240 所房屋被毁。

到周二中午，消防队员已经在该地区的不同地区进行干预，以扑灭再次发生的火灾。

一名 23 岁男子因涉嫌在瓦尔地区纵火而被捕。目前面临15年监禁。内政部长洛朗·努涅斯表示，自 7 月 6 日以来，已有 184 人因与火灾有关而被捕。

致波尔多西南部比斯卡罗斯地区消防员的信息

皮克卡尤酒庄 (Château Picque Caillou) 是波尔多西区为数不多的几家葡萄酒庄园之一，其总经理佩吉·普卢希内克 (Peggy Plouhinec) 告诉 BBC，由于烟雾，她的生意选择在周末关门，但自那以后情况有所改善，周日晚上的一场降雨也起到了帮助作用。

虽然她的葡萄园没有面临风险，但她说游客已经“抛弃”了该地区。

“今年夏天，酒店业将受到影响，这是肯定的，”她补充道。 “正在发生的事情是前所未有的。我们很幸运，还没有受到太大影响，但业务仍将因游客数量减少而受到影响。”

“但许多人失去了家园或生意，更不用说已经辛苦工作了数周、肯定已经筋疲力尽的消防员了。”

上周晚些时候撤离的卡普费雷特的一名居民告诉法国媒体，他现在主要担心的是他所居住的半岛，而不是内陆的大城市。

“每个人都在谈论拯救波尔多，但波尔多除了混凝土什么都没有。你见过混凝土燃烧吗？”

“这里只有树木……当你看到所有东西都被烧毁时，那就是一场灾难。”
